rationale: Direct examination of the foundational paper by Chelban et al. (2017, PMID: 28575651) confirms that the initial cohort comprised exactly seven affected individuals from three families, rather than 14 individuals from 8 families. The subsequent 2020 study by Chelban et al. (PMID: 31509304) identified 11 new cases from eight families, clarifying any potential conflation of cohort sizes across publications.

evidence.text: The original study by Chelban et al. explicitly describes 7 affected individuals from 3 families of different ethnic backgrounds presenting with early-onset spastic ataxia and hypomyelination due to bi-allelic NKX6-2 mutations.

source.title: Mutations in NKX6-2 Cause Progressive Spastic Ataxia and Hypomyelination
source.journal: The American Journal of Human Genetics
source.quote: We report seven individuals with an early-onset spastic-ataxia phenotype. The individuals come from three families of different ethnic backgrounds.

evidence.text: Chelban et al. (2020) later reported an expanded multicentre cohort consisting of 11 new affected individuals from 8 unrelated families, confirming that the 8-family figure belongs to the 2020 follow-up series and not the foundational 2017 paper.

source.title: Genetic and phenotypic characterization of NKX6‐2‐related spastic ataxia and hypomyelination
source.quote: Eleven new cases from eight families of different ethnic backgrounds carrying compound heterozygous and homozygous pathogenic variants in NKX6-2 were identified...

new_directions.question_text: What are the exact phenotype frequencies (e.g., nystagmus, spasticity, hypomyelination) across the pooled worldwide cohort of all published NKX6-2 patients to date?
new_directions.rationale: Compiling an updated meta-analysis of all reported NKX6-2 patients from 2017 through current literature will establish standardized HPO term frequencies to enhance clinical differential diagnosis against Pelizaeus-Merzbacher-like disease and other AR spastic ataxias.
